title: Performance harness target routes, SIT identity set and pipeline stage are not named for the microservice target
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Technical Enabler Stories v7.md (RWB-TE-009 sections 3, 12 and 13)
description: The legacy story fixes the load (410 virtual users at 3 requests a minute), the pass criteria (95th percentile under 2,000 ms, error rate under 1 percent) and the operations exercised, but the microservice target names neither the gateway-bff composite routes behind the screens, nor the SIT identity groups and test users (it cites DL40, which is not in the source set), nor the pipeline stage that runs the harness. The harness is a pipeline stage and provides no REST operation of its own, so contract tables 12.1 and 12.3 to 12.8 are empty by design.
evidence: RWB-TE-009 section 3 bullet 2 (roles.txt and Entra ID groups per DL40), section 12 (operations exercised on the monolith base) and section 13 (perf/recovery folder, not part of the deployed service); Arch v5 slide 20 (gateway-bff is the only entry for staff screens) and slide 48 (414 concurrent staff at peak, about 21 requests a second).
proposed: Fix the composite route list, the SIT identity groups and the pipeline stage name at the harness configuration review before the first SIT run; keep every value in configuration, never in the script.

title: Browser stage screen routes, Thai and English label source and scan engine are not named for the microservice edge
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Technical Enabler Stories v7.md (RWB-TE-010 sections 3, 11, 12, 13 and 15)
section: 3 Preconditions; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: The legacy story fixes the six screens and their states, the four browser configurations (current and previous major versions of Microsoft Edge and Google Chrome), the WCAG 2.1 A and AA scan and the Thai and English check. The microservice target names neither the gateway-bff composite routes behind the six screens, nor the owner of the Thai and English label values (reference data of rwb-case under DP-07), nor the scan engine and the stage name. The runner is a pipeline stage and provides no REST operation of its own.
evidence: RWB-TE-010 section 3 (runner image, browsers.json, DL37), section 11 (role_code, label_en and label_th), section 12 (screens.json, browsers.json, a11y-exceptions.json) and section 15 (six screens and their states); Arch v5 slide 20 (gateway-bff is the only entry for staff screens); ownership map lov_value and reference_row owner P3.
proposed: Fix the composite route list, the label source and the scan engine at the browser-stage configuration review before the first SIT run; keep the browser list and the exception list in configuration.
